correctness.rationale: A committee fails the integral Hare core exactly when a proposal of size t has at least nt/k strictly improving voters. Under candidate exchangeability, disjoint equal-sized candidate blocks force the proposed block to be a unique strict maximum among floor(k/t)+1 exchangeable counts, giving improvement probability at most 1/(floor(k/t)+1). Exact integer arithmetic gives minimum quota gap 1/[k(k+1)]. Total variation controls the averaged improvement probability under heterogeneous ballots; independence, Jensen and Chernoff yield the finite bound. A biased one-hot multinomial model proves sharpness at and above the boundary, and a binomial sandwich yields the exact logarithmic large-deviation rate. Exact checker passes 446363 orbit comparisons, 6678 direct core-profile checks and 14 TV identities; finite checks are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem scope and implication direction were compared to five primary papers, including the full relevant model and existence results of arXiv:2609.11912 and the random AJR paper arXiv:2510.18718. None of the inspected claims includes an aggregate-symmetry TV radius for *all* integral Hare-core committees, its non-iid Chernoff bound, or the sharp one-hot boundary. Multiple scientific search formulations and available prior claims were checked. Novelty remains best-knowledge and not independently established.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently worded average-case core results may be equivalent; web and semantic search coverage is not exhaustive.
Only relevant sections, rather than every appendix, were inspected for some less-plausible related sources.
The exact sharp TV radius is uniform over candidate counts and approval laws; individual specific laws may tolerate larger deviations.

value.rationale: The core is a demanding fairness selection criterion and recent work solves only the deterministic existence question. The theorem identifies a qualitatively different symmetry regime in which *every* committee is stable, shows this degeneracy is exponentially robust under heterogeneous voter laws and within-ballot correlation, and derives the sharp quantitative contamination radius at which the phenomenon ceases. The exact one-hot large-deviation boundary supplies a natural benchmark for detecting when core stability becomes discriminating. The conclusion is a motivated structural and phase-transition result, not a numerical increment or an arbitrary finite slice.
